news.title: USWNT embarks on Women's World Cup qualification at the CONCACAF W Championship
news.lede: The pursuit of a fifth Women's World Cup title begins in earnest for the U.S. national team on Friday. The United States will play El Salvador in the quarterfinals of the CONCACAF W Championship, which serves as the confederation’s qualifying tournament for next year’s World Cup in Brazil. news.title: Former Ferns coach Tom Sermanni helps PNG chase World Cup dream
news.lede: Former Football Ferns head coach Tom Sermanni is helping Papua New Guinea prepare for their bid to reach the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. The experienced Scottish coach has joined PNG’s technical support team as they prepare for three intercontinental play-off matches in Morocco. Sermanni (72) and fellow technical expert Mark Arnot have spent recent months working with PNG’s coaching staff in Port Moresby. Main photo: Tom Sermanni … another World Cup campaign.

news.title: Arsenal face possible ban from FIFA competitions - 'We have the power to act'
news.lede: The Independent Football Regulator has warned Arsenal and other Premier League giants that they could be excluded from future editions of FIFA tournaments if they disrupt the English calendar. That includes the coveted Club World Cup , which takes place once every four years outside of the usual Premier League season. Scheduling conflicts could jeopardise the participation of clubs like the Gunners, Manchester United and Liverpool moving forward - despite Chelsea winning last summer's maiden instalment of a 32-team competition. Regulator chair David Kogan told a Digital, Culture, Media and Sport committee: "There are clearly signs taking place from other entities - and FIFA is the obvious one - where it's creating global club competitions that currently sit outside the normal season of the English game and are every four years.

news.title: Uli Hoeneß takes jab at Julian Nagelsmann’s handling of World Cup
news.lede: Uli Hoeneß is already making it pretty clear what he expects from Jürgen Klopp’s Germany tenure, and there might be a little side-eye directed toward the previous regime in the process.
